title: Aphorism § 188
text:
§ 188



These affections were considered to be merely topical, and were
          therefore called local diseases, as if they were maladies exclusively limited to those
          parts wherein the organism took little or no part, or affections of these particular
          visible parts of which the rest of the living organism, so to speak, knew nothing. 1


1  One of the many great and pernicious blunders of the old
          school.
